title: From b-Coloring to $b^*$-Coloring: Large Girth and Parameterized Complexity
summary: A b-coloring is a proper vertex coloring such that every color class contains a vertex, a so-called b-vertex, which sees all colors in its closed neighborhood. This type of coloring has been intensively studied from both structural and algorithmic point of view. Recently, Zaker [DAM 2025] introduced the notion of a b*-coloring, which is a b-coloring in which there is a vertex that sees a b-vertex of every color in its closed neighborhood.
